Or it says plainly, in its title or its summary, that it is a kind of place and names no premises: then `place.name` holds the kind, for example `motel`, and `place.locality` the town. Where you are given places to stay from map data for a town, a premises you name there is one of those, under the name it is given, if any of them fits the party. A kind of place is the fallback, for a town whose list is empty or where nothing in it fits.

Access needs: not answered
Budget: shoestring, as a feeling rather than a figure
Appetite for effort: demanding
Roughest night they will accept: rustic
Would rule the trip out: Nothing that requires a river ford above the knee

About this backcountry:
Nights away from a road: 3

Most they will walk in a day: 16 km
Experience: some

candidatesAccepted.title: Refuge huts on the International Appalachian Trail, Parc national de la Gaspésie
candidatesAccepted.summary: Rustic Sépaq backcountry refuges (bunks, wood stove, no electricity) along the well-marked IAT/SIA, which suits a hut-based trip with days up to 16 km. Huts are reserved per night through Sépaq and fill early in late summer. Access needs were not answered and are not accounted for. Specific refuges and ford conditions were not checked, so confirm with the park that the chosen segments have no knee-deep crossings and are marked well enough for cloud.

candidatesAccepted.title: Camping at Gîte du Mont-Albert campground area, Parc national de la Gaspésie
candidatesAccepted.summary: A cheap road-accessible night at the park's central sector before or after the hut nights. It gives the party a base to check the weather forecast before committing to exposed summits. Season dates and accessibility were not checked.

candidatesAccepted.title: Budget motel in Sainte-Anne-des-Monts
candidatesAccepted.summary: A low-cost roof on the way in from Québec City, about 40 km from the park entrance. It breaks up the long drive and offers a fallback if cloud makes the high trails unwise. No specific premises were given, so this is a kind of place rather than a named one.

candidatesAccepted.title: Mont Jacques-Cartier summit hike
candidatesAccepted.summary: Highest summit in southern Québec, alpine tundra and a chance of seeing the caribou herd; the trail is well marked, which suits a party that would rather not navigate in cloud. Access is sometimes restricted for caribou protection, and the shuttle or parking arrangement is not accounted for here. Access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Mont Albert loop via the summit plateau
candidatesAccepted.summary: Demanding loop of roughly 17 km across a serpentine tableland plateau. That is slightly over the party's 16 km daily limit, so it fits better if broken at a backcountry hut. The plateau is exposed and cloud-prone; turning back in poor visibility is wise. Ford conditions were not checked. Access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Night in a park backcountry hut (refuge)
candidatesAccepted.summary: Rustic huts along the International Appalachian Trail make a hut-to-hut route possible within the 16 km daily limit. Which huts, the distances between them, and any river crossings were not verified; check the official route notes for fords above the knee. Huts likely need reserving well ahead for late summer. Access needs were not answered.

place.name: Parc national de la Gaspésie backcountry huts

candidatesAccepted.title: Lac aux Américains short hike
candidatesAccepted.summary: A short, sheltered hike to a glacial cirque lake. It is a good low-visibility fallback for a cloudy day, with little navigation needed. Access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Mont Jacques-Cartier summit conditions and caribou-zone rules
candidatesAccepted.summary: An above-treeline summit that is exposed to fast-moving cloud, wind and cold even in late August, so pack a waterproof shell, an insulating layer, a hat and gloves. Access is regulated to protect the caribou, and trail openings can change. Check current trail status and access rules with Sépaq (Parc national de la Gaspésie) before setting out. This is not clearance to go. Access needs were not answered, so I could not account for them.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hut-based alpine plateau traverse with a cloud-day fallback
candidatesAccepted.summary: Sépaq huts (refuges) make a rustic, shoestring-friendly base for demanding days within your 16 km limit. The tundra plateaus can lose visibility quickly, and you would rather not navigate in cloud. Carry a map, a compass and a GPS track as backups, and pick hut links where you can descend below treeline if the cloud comes in. Hut fees here are an estimate, not a quote. Confirm availability, rates and trail status with Sépaq.

candidatesAccepted.title: Pre-trip forecast check for the Chic-Chocs
candidatesAccepted.summary: Late August to mid-September brings cool nights that can drop near freezing up high, along with rain bands and strong summit winds. Use Environment and Climate Change Canada's Gaspésie forecasts and ask at the park's Discovery and Visitors Centre for current conditions and any stream crossings. Do not go if a crossing would mean fording above the knee. This is a conditions pointer, not clearance to go.

candidatesAccepted.title: Reserve backcountry hut nights with Sépaq
candidatesAccepted.summary: Hut (refuge) nights in Parc national de la Gaspésie are reserved through Sépaq and popular late-summer weekends fill early; securing three consecutive rustic hut nights within 16 km legs is what decides whether this trip happens. Exact hut nightly rates and current availability were not checked, and access needs were not answered, so hut accessibility is unaccounted for. Fording conditions on the chosen huts' routes should be confirmed with the park, since knee-deep crossings rule the trip out.

candidatesAccepted.summary: Québec national parks charge a daily access fee per adult, and overnight backcountry users register before heading out; it is also where to ask about current trail and river conditions. Exact current fee and registration procedure were not verified.

candidatesAccepted.title: Offline maps and an emergency satellite messenger
candidatesAccepted.summary: Cell coverage in the Chic-Chocs is very limited, and since neither of you has navigated in cloud, carrying offline topo maps plus a rented or owned satellite messenger gives a way to call for help if fog rolls in. Rental availability in Québec City was not checked.

candidatesAccepted.title: Check travel insurance covers backcountry rescue
candidatesAccepted.summary: Confirm that your provincial health plan and any travel or accident policy cover search, rescue and evacuation from remote terrain; out-of-province residents especially should check. Your residency and existing coverage were not given, so the cost band is a rough guess.
